answer: Per-epoch puzzle plus a locked bond makes each agent identity cost money up front: a new Sybil must solve a fresh challenge and post collateral before any answer counts, so one thousand fakes pay one thousand puzzles and stakes instead of sharing one. Grading compares submissions, and a near-duplicate is an echo of the original, flagged and unpaid. A farm therefore leaves a hollow trail of identical text that earns nothing, while a lone honest agent describing a lagoon survey keeps its reward. Break-even needs the cluster to out-earn forfeited stakes, so mass registration stays unprofitable.
